subject: general
question: Which of the following 'indicators' is used to test the nature of solutions besides litmus paper?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Turmeric and red cabbage juice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **indicator** is a special substance that changes its color when exposed to an **acidic** or **basic** medium, thereby helping to determine the chemical nature of a solution.
 
• **Turmeric** is a very common **natural indicator**. It contains a yellow pigment called **curcumin**. In **acidic** and **neutral** solutions, turmeric remains **yellow**, but it turns **reddish-brown** when it comes into contact with a **base** (such as soap solution). ***Hence, the option containing turmeric is correct.***
 
• **Red cabbage juice** is another effective **natural indicator** derived from the leaves of red cabbage. It contains **anthocyanin** molecules that change color depending on pH. It turns **red or pink** in **acidic** solutions, **purple** in **neutral** solutions, and **green or yellow** in **basic** solutions. ***Hence, the option containing red cabbage juice is correct.***
 
• Substances like **sand**, **alcohol**, **sugar**, **water**, and **table salt** are not indicators because they do not change color in a predictable way to signify the presence of hydrogen ions (acids) or hydroxide ions (bases).
 
• Other natural indicators include **China Rose (Gudhal)**, which turns **dark pink (magenta)** in **acidic** solutions and **green** in **basic** solutions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Natural Indicators:**
 
 
• **Litmus**: Extracted from **Lichens**, it is the most commonly used indicator. It is **purple** in distilled water, turns **red** in **acidic** solutions, and **blue** in **basic** solutions.
 
• **Onion and Vanilla**: These are known as **Olfactory Indicators**. Their **characteristic smell** changes or disappears when mixed with **acids** or **bases**, which is particularly useful for visually impaired students.
 
 
 
• **Synthetic Indicators:**
 
 
• **Phenolphthalein**: This is a man-made indicator that remains **colorless** in **acidic** solutions but turns **deep pink** in **basic** solutions.
 
• **Methyl Orange**: Another synthetic indicator that shows a **red** color in **acidic** media and a **yellow** color in **basic** media.
 
 
 
• **The pH Scale:**
 
 
• The concept of **pH** was introduced by **S.P.L. Sorensen** in **1909** to measure the **acidity** or **alkalinity** of a substance.
 
• The scale ranges from **0 to 14**. A **pH of 7** is considered **neutral** (e.g., **pure water**). A **pH less than 7** indicates an **acid**, while a **pH greater than 7** indicates a **base**.
 
• **Universal Indicator**: This is a mixture of several indicators that shows different colors at different **concentrations of hydrogen ions** in a solution, providing a more precise pH value than simple litmus paper.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reaction of Acids and Bases**: When an acid and a base react, they undergo a **neutralization reaction** to form **salt and water**. Indicators are often used in **titrations** to find the **equivalence point** of this reaction.
 
• **Everyday Examples**: The **reddish-brown stain** of turmeric on a white shirt turns **yellow** again when washed with plenty of water or treated with an **acid** like **lemon juice**, illustrating the reversible nature of the indicator's color change.
 
• **Anthocyanins**: These are the pigments found in **Red Cabbage**, **Blueberries**, and **Raspberries** that provide their vibrant colors and serve as pH-sensitive chemical sensors.
</ul
